componentImages.name: +5VDC
componentImages.note:
The user port is a very convenient place to measure the voltages coming from the PSU. If the +5VDC is within a reasonable tolerance of +5V (approximately 4.7V to 5.2V), you can be fairly confident that the PSU is supplying the correct voltage.

On C64 long‑board you should also verify the +5VDC “CAN” rail (VR2) and the +12VDC rail (VR1).

componentImages.name: 9VAC
componentImages.note: The user port is a very convenient place to measure the voltages coming from the PSU, and the 9VAC is coming (almost) directly from the PSU

componentImages.name: Pinout
componentImages.note:
C64 has two +5VDC power supplies:

1) One that comes directly from the power supply, which powers most IC's.

2) One being converted on mainboard from 9VAC (called "CAN"), which powers the more sensitive components like VIC and system clocks.

scopeBaselines.name: SYNC/LUM explanation
scopeBaselines.note:
Measuring the SYNC/LUMA signal, is a fairly good indicator if the screen is being generated correctly. In this example we can see how the standard blue screen with BASIC looks like.

Put your scope to ~20μS, where you should see the draw of ~4 lines on the screen. 

The red box is one row of the screen.

Screen row 1: 
1 = Black left-side border
2 = White line at left-side of screen
3 = Lightblue left-side border 
4 = Darkblue middle area
5 = Lightblue right-side border 
6 = Black right-side

Screen row 2 (besides the above stuff):
7 = Text on screen

In this example we can see a little more than 4 screen rows.
